questionText:
Let $R_i(z)$ and $W_i(z)$ denote read and write operations on a data element $z$ by a transaction $T_i$, respectively. Consider the schedule $S$ with four transactions.

$$S: R_4(x)R_2(x)R_3(x)R_1(y)W_1(y)W_2(x)W_3(y)R_4(y)$$

Which one of the following serial schedules is conflict equivalent to $S$?
explanation:
To find the conflict equivalent serial schedule, we construct a precedence (precedence/serialization) graph by identifying all conflicting operations (operations on the same data item by different transactions where at least one operation is a write):

1. Conflicting operations on data element $x$:
• $R_4(x)$ followed by $W_2(x) \Rightarrow T_4 \rightarrow T_2$
• $R_3(x)$ followed by $W_2(x) \Rightarrow T_3 \rightarrow T_2$

2. Conflicting operations on data element $y$:
• $R_1(y)$ followed by $W_3(y) \Rightarrow T_1 \rightarrow T_3$
• $W_1(y)$ followed by $W_3(y) \Rightarrow T_1 \rightarrow T_3$
• $W_1(y)$ followed by $R_4(y) \Rightarrow T_1 \rightarrow T_4$
• $W_3(y)$ followed by $R_4(y) \Rightarrow T_3 \rightarrow T_4$

Edges in Precedence Graph:
• $T_1 \rightarrow T_3$
• $T_1 \rightarrow T_4$
• $T_3 \rightarrow T_4$
• $T_3 \rightarrow T_2$
• $T_4 \rightarrow T_2$

Performing a topological sort on these edges:
• $T_1$ has an in-degree of 0, so it executes first: $T_1$
• $T_3$ now has an in-degree of 0, so it executes next: $T_3$
• $T_4$ now has an in-degree of 0, so it executes next: $T_4$
• $T_2$ executes last: $T_2$

Thus, the conflict equivalent serial schedule is $T_1 \rightarrow T_3 \rightarrow T_4 \rightarrow T_2$.
